 Shorthanded, travel-delayed Bulls fend off Timberwolves for second-straight win
 Despite no Jalen Smith, no Nic Claxton, and a hectic travel delay that caused the Bulls to land in Minneapolis just a few hours before the game, the Bulls earned their second-straight victory with a 117-106 win over the Timberwolves on Saturday night.
 Sam Smith November 15, 2026 9:37 AM CST NBA history is rich with special teams, like our choice for the best ever: the 1996 72-win NBA champion Bulls.
 Then there’s Bill Russell’s 60s dynasty Celtics, the best to sustain. Arguably the best to put on a show, Magic’s 80s Lakers.
 So could these Bulls distinguish themselves as maybe the best 3-9 team?
 They sure looked like it on Saturday during the most difficult of circumstances in a 117-106 victory over the presumably contending Minnesota Timberwolves.
 Not only did the Bulls lead for all but the first three minutes and by double digit margins in each quarter, but the Bulls did so against a rested Timberwolves team with the league’s top rated defense on a long home stand. While the Bulls not only were completing the second of a back to back duo without their top two centers, injured Jalen Smith and Nic Claxton, but enduring complicated travel difficulties due to the nationwide flight shutdown that pushed their Friday night departure to Saturday. And a subsequent delay that resulted in the team arriving in Minneapolis just a few hours before the start of the game.
 And as a side note, maybe the Bulls also provided a major service to the NBA. Call them the No Excuses Bulls.
 If they can play like this with all that, enough of the load management.
 Back to back, shorthanded, finally winning a game after losing eight straight. This looked like it was going to be like waking up and your phone battery was dead, you couldn’t find the car keys, the dog couldn’t hold it in, the cop said 35 is 35 and you are getting a ticket for going 40, and you really need a rest room. And you still have to go to... Minnesota in November?
 So maybe it really is, like Yogi Berra said, 90 percent mental while the other half is physical.
 The Bulls, yes the Bulls, were tougher and more physical, out rebounding the Timberwolves of stone hands Rudy Gobert. The Bulls were smarter, though that’s a low bar against a team led by LaMelo Ball, who shot seven of 25 overall and four of 19 on threes, and flat footed and dumbfounded — at least us — continued to jack ‘em up to the end. Like he probably said, they all felt good leaving my hand.
 The Bulls were dominant in leading by 16 points with under four minutes remaining in the game, but then they had a Ballesque brain lock and allowed seven straight points. Until saved (again?) by Patrick Williams with a steal from former teammate Ayo Dosunmu and a send-em-to-the-exits three for a season-best 14 points that with a minute left effectively clinched a game the ‘wolves were favored to win by 16 points.
 Norman Powell led the Bulls with 24 points and Matas Buzelis had his most efficient and effective game of the season with 18 points on nine shots with a team high nine rebounds. Buddy Hield and Tre Jones, both deftly cycling in off the bench to spread out the playing time, each scored 16 points for a Bulls reserves’ 50-33 edge. Williams, Jones and Hield were the team’s plus/minus leaders. Dosunmu led Minnesota with 24 points, 14 in a third quarter scare when the Timberwolves cut a 15-point Bulls halftime lead to one.
 But as the Bulls would do throughout this game when threatened, after that third quarter ‘wolves’ howl, the Bulls made the big play, often a steal, offensive rebound or clutch shot. It was that laser quick release from Hield for a 17 footer. Then Williams was fouled grabbing a rebound of a Jones miss, Williams with a steal from Illini Terrence Shannon that turned into a Jones layup, Hield with a three, all six feet of Jones blocking a Shannon drive. And Williams knifing in for a dunk on a pass from emergency starter Zach Collins. Who, by the way, if Gobert is a Defensive Player of the Year candidate, Collins could be Defensive Player of the Century in relentlessly turning away Gobert’s feeble scoring attempts. The Frenchman of little resistance was zero for seven on attempted bunnies and other foraging attempts.
 You could have done your own Where’s Rudy puzzle book the way the Bulls had 30 points in the paint by halftime.
 Okay, maybe Defensive Player of the Night for Zach, but we hadn’t been seeing much winning and it’s just such a nice change.
 Scare managed, Bulls back ahead by eight points going into the fourth quarter.
 Yes, I also know that 16 points wagering guess is just two possessions in the NFL. But maybe it’s a kick in the butt and kick start for a Bulls team that many felt were punting the season.
 Winning streak, anyone?
 “Kudos to the group,” commended Bulls coach Tiago Splitter. “That win last night (against Atlanta) helped us to bring the mojo back a little bit. Even with guys out, traveling today. No excuses, the guys brought it. A lot of guys helped with this win. Got to keep building from this. Fresh legs, playing fast, trying to beat them with our game. That second unit in the third quarter was great because we started so so the third quarter again. But the second unit brought it and played well.
 “Finally we are making some shots; that helps of course,” Splitter added, the Bulls almost 50 percent on threes again after spending the first 10 games at the clank bank.
 “One of the things I tell the guys every day, you still have to bring it, you still have to play the right way when the shots don’t fall. I think we are doing that now,” said Splitter.
 It also was something of a subtle masterclass from the understated Splitter.
 Not only about the team’s compete level remaining high despite the 1-9 start and injury loss of star rookie Caleb Wilson for at least a month with a broken hand. And not only the way Splitter slyly manipulated the rotation against Minnesota like a relay race to keep fresh legs and active bodies on the Timberwolves players. Who seemed awfully disjointed. And which you can’t completely deny had a lot to do with the Bulls. Ball’s oddball shooting choices can impact a lot. But the Timberwolves were held to their fewest points of the season and lowest scoring first period in the 29-17 Bulls lead.
 No one is about to mistake these Bulls for the ’91 Dobermans. But there were closeouts without flybys, screens navigated and so much crashing they were checking for broken dishes in the kitchen. 
 It was just a hungry Bulls team. Who, indeed, let the dawgs out?
 “Looking at ourselves in the mirror: Are we going to be the team everybody thinks is our lunch? Or play for each other and compete,” wondered Hield. “Where the only thing that matters is not who has the highest number in the box score, but getting Ws.”
 Cool Hand Tiago does not have a failure to communicate.
 Hield is among several Bulls who have gone from regulars to rotation to relegated. All the while remaining prepared and returning to produce. As Hield and Williams did against the Timberwolves.
 “Pat we know besides what has happened in the past we flushed,” said Hield. “This league is what have you done for me lately, and what Pat has done lately is tremendous; we’re going to keep building off that. Trusting Tiago and his decision making. Whether we like it or not, it’s not our job. We go out there and compete and be a supportive teammate, and then when our number gets called, go out there and compete. We’ve got to be professionals and treat this like a job and be the best teammate we can be even when we’re not playing. So just trying to find ways to contribute. It’s fun being out there and it’s fun winning.”
 Splitter also did something subtlety subtle that everyone calls for, coaches like to say they do, but few follow through. I know there’s song lyrics in there somewhere, but I have to move on.
 Perhaps it was a rotation for a tired team or to protect a player who’d been out as Powell was two games with back spasms. But after a Ben Johnson first quarter from the starting blocks for the Bulls again like Friday against Atlanta — Minnesota missing its first 13 threes after Atlanta three of 17 to begin the game— Minnesota began to make a law of averages few and got within 36-28 four minutes into the second quarter. Powell then dribbled around and took a forced three, and a few seconds later Splitter substituted Hield for Powell and left the other four starters in the game.
 No, we’re not playing that way.
 Message sent. Powell returned to the game about five minutes later, and his next two shot attempts were driving scores. Heck of a message sent. And received. Nothing personal. You’ll go back in.
 That’s not how we play. And a player who understood and effectively agreed.
 Which seemed to the Bulls benefit at variance with Minnesota when Ball kept returning to the game and taking even more egregious threes. Heck, Hornets management may get executive of the year getting off that more than $40 million per. The Timberwolves had won five straight games and now are 9-4, so maybe just a bad night. And maybe Anthony Edwards is enough gauze to cover up their wounds when he eventually returns from injury in a few months. It’s still a good team.
 That the Bulls made look very ordinary.
 Though you still had flashbacks of those early season Bulls collapses.
 It did seem these Bulls were coming even in some of the losses like when they blew big leads against the 76ers and Spurs. But that record.
 And here of all guys came our beloved Ayo, waking up the Timberwolves with so many of those uncanny drives that we just couldn’t believe he beat everyone with. It was the first real spirit the Timberwolves showed in the game. And suddenly that 58-45 Bulls halftime lead was down to 65-64 midway through the third quarter.
 When the ‘wolves awakened that sleeping giant?
 Patrick Williams?
 Well, sleeping was an adjective often hurled derisively. Though Williams lately has been a surprise — at least to many — vital component in these wins after starting the season with seven straight DNPs by coach.
 “As I’ve been telling you (media) guys the whole season, he brings it every day,” Splitter insisted about Williams. “He’s been awesome. Even when he was not playing he was ready and being active and now he is playing well for us, and finishing games for us. I thought he was a big part, got a huge block at the end and a huge three to seal the game. His energy on the bench, the locker room; he’s one of those positive vibes guys. And he made four threes tonight and was very important for us and he’s going to continue to do that.”
 Another Splitter miracle?
 Anyway, here was Williams at that pivotal time in the third quarter trying to nudge Dosunmu away from a loose ball going out of bounds when the official caught Williams shoving the ball into Dosunmu’s chest. It looked playful at first, two old buddies, though we also know Ayo isn’t the quiet kid next door he appears to be. He’s got an edge and unloads his share of trash talk, and Williams apparently didn’t like it. It’s part of why Ayo is so accomplished despite not necessarily being the most skilled player. Tougher than he looks.
 Maybe Pat, too.
 There’s an old rock and roll song about a girl who tells her boyfriend she’s breaking up to get him to show some emotion.
 “Johnny get angry
Johnny get mad
Give me the biggest lecture that I ever had
I want a brave man
I want a cave man
Johnny show me that you care, really care for me”
 Patrick Williams cares.
 After the technical foul, believed to be the third in Williams’ career, he rebounded a Jones miss and was fouled, making two free throws, made a steal from Shannon leading to a Jones three-point play and a driving dunk from a Collins pass.
 And then even though that reserve group paused briefly, Splitter basically closed the game with Williams and the reserves as Williams, like Buzelis against Atlanta, drove in the final stake with a three pointer with a minute left after the still fighting’ Illini of Dosunmu and Shannon got within 113-106 with just over a minute left.
 Which was just after one of my favorite parts of the game when it looked like after all the mayhem the Timberwolves might just win one they didn’t deserve. Minnesota was gnawing at the rope, within eight points with about nine minutes left and perhaps the Bulls might let go. Ball swiped the rock from Powell — Ball ballin’ stealing the ball? — and suddenly was leading a three-on-one. When Ball decided rather than to take the easy score and maybe that big mo he threw a wild high alley-oop oops lob attempt that Jonathan Kuminga couldn’t handle. 
 And maybe the Bulls were boring closing it out with accurate shooting and backboard mastery. But nobody was yawning about another win.
